problem: The ticket's source wording describes a V1/V2 cross-workspace boundary that no longer exists in the consolidated repository. The remaining problem is to state this three-field contract in authoritative architecture documentation and retain a deterministic regression proof; the historical fabricated-field override is evidence of a past defect, not current behavior.
value: Preserving the existing minimal three-field application projection prevents future matcher changes from silently consuming absent or fabricated profile values. This specification separates already-present source behavior from the remaining documentation and mutation-proof work without claiming either has been completed.
desiredOutcome: The architecture record names the canonical root packages and accurately documents the current three-field application projection and call direction; an isolated planned regression demonstrates that adding a fourth-field read fails typechecking and that restoring the source returns the baseline to green. No runtime shape, scoring, API, or persistence behavior changes in this ticket.
inScope: Document and test the existing `MatchingProfile` to `MatchableProfile` compile-time boundary across the canonical root workspace. Preserve the `expectedCtc`, `yearsOfExperience`, and `willingToRelocate` projection and persisted per-search snapshot semantics.
functionalRequirements: The source title and portions of its evidence retain versioned-workspace wording from before the completed single-codebase consolidation. Treat those statements as historical provenance, not current architecture: active paths are `packages/core/src/profile.ts`, `packages/shared/src/types.ts`, `packages/matching/src/context.ts`, and `apps/workers/search/src/collect.ts`; no active `v2/` package tree exists.

Current code already narrows both application shapes to the same three fields and passes the MatchingProfile directly; source history records the prior fabricated-field override and its removal. Distinguish that existing evidence from the still-required architecture-record review and not-yet-run mutation proof; do not report the old failure mode as a currently reproduced runtime defect.

The compile-time contract is specifically the application subobject passed from `MatchingProfile` to `buildCandidateContext`: it exposes only `expectedCtc`, `yearsOfExperience`, and `willingToRelocate`. The matching consumer may not read a fourth application field unless the canonical snapshot contract is deliberately reviewed and updated.

`buildCandidateContext` has a separate optional `resumeText` parameter whose default is an empty string; the search worker currently calls `buildCandidateContext(profile)` without passing raw resume text. CS-78 specifies only the typed MatchingProfile/application boundary and does not claim to redesign or prove all resume-text handling elsewhere in the matching system.

Preserve the deliberately minimal snapshot created by `matchingProfile`; do not pass or serialize `currentCtc`, `noticePeriodDays`, or the full writable `ApplicationDetails` into matching to silence a type error.

At the search-worker call site, pass the typed `MatchingProfile` directly to the matcher. Do not add `as MatchableProfile`, `as any`, fabricated fallback fields, or a second projection that changes scoring inputs.

Reconcile historical V1/V2 names and paths in the source acceptance criteria against the current one-workspace architecture: document `packages/core`, `packages/shared`, `packages/matching`, and `apps/workers/search` as the active boundary; do not reintroduce versioned workspaces or file dependencies as an implementation requirement.

A mutation proving the boundary must be isolated from the developer checkout: make `packages/matching/src/context.ts` read a fourth application property absent from `MatchableProfile`, require the canonical typecheck to fail with the property diagnostic at the consumer, restore the mutation, and require the same typecheck to pass. Record both outcomes; a pass-only run is insufficient.

This is a data contract, not JavaScript runtime immutability (`Object.freeze`). Keep this direction and the structural TypeScript boundary; do not add an API, service, endpoint, or new persistence field.

Dialog-specific focus management applies only to dialog primitives; manual screen-reader judgment remains a separate required evidence gate.
responsive: Validate reflow at 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440 CSS pixels; ordinary content must not horizontally overflow. Maintain touch-usable controls and long-content wrapping; do not assert locale support beyond installed English copy.
browsers: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit verification for shared controls and visual snapshots at agreed desktop/mobile viewport; snapshots must identify browser/font versions and deterministic masks.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: INPUT_VALIDATION / PRIVACY_PII. UI primitives are not authorization controls; server-side endpoint permissions remain authoritative. Never embed secrets, PII, resumes, fake metrics or user data in tokens, examples, screenshots or story fixtures. Avoid unsafe HTML injection and remote assets; CSP/local asset policy remains in force.
observability: NOT_APPLICABLE to static tokens/primitives: no telemetry is added. Runtime consuming features retain their existing redacted request/error logging contract; do not log component props or personal data.
manualExternalGates: HUMAN_VALIDATION: UX/product review of approved reference parity and tolerance; manual NVDA or VoiceOver smoke test after implementation. These are future evidence and are not completed by generating this specification.
implementationChecklist: Inventory existing global tokens/primitives and their consumers; record duplicates or gaps before changing style ownership.
Map approved canonical palette/type/spacing/responsive/focus/motion references to semantic CSS tokens; retain explicit legacy compatibility only where migration has an identified consumer.
Implement shared atoms and state variants from the atomic component hierarchy only where current canonical product surfaces consume them.
Replace route-local primitive duplication with shared components only within approved implementation scope; preserve behavior and existing API ownership.
Add rendered component tests for applicable states, keyboard/a11y assertions and privacy sentinels; do not use screenshot samples as live content.
Run visual comparisons in Chromium/Firefox/WebKit at exact approved viewports and document tool versions, tolerance and masks.
Complete manual design and screen-reader review; reconcile docs and evidence against the exact reviewed implementation SHA.
risksRecovery: Over-broad token replacement may cause visual regressions or break legacy surfaces; migrate consumers incrementally, compare approved reference and retain reversible CSS/consumer changes. A visual pass cannot waive keyboard, privacy or server authorization requirements.
definitionOfDone: Implementation DoD: canonical tokens match approved source, primitives expose only applicable documented states, route consumers share components without regression, all AC state/viewport/browser evidence is current, visual tolerances are explicit, automated accessibility/privacy/keyboard tests pass, and UX plus manual screen-reader review is recorded. Release DoD also requires exact-SHA hosted CI and product acceptance. Specification completion alone does not activate or promote the R1 ticket.

problem: A Cognito rollout can lock out candidates or disclose identity material if disposable-flow behavior, provider limits, exact deployed revision and rollback are not verified before enabling it. The current decision and optional code are not hosted rollout proof.
value: Make any future identity-provider activation a reversible, monitored release decision backed by disposable-account and exact-revision evidence.
functionalRequirements: AC1 runs only against an isolated disposable user/pool/mailbox after CS-90..CS-93 prerequisites are accepted; never use the owner or candidate account. Matrix must cover email signup, OTP success, wrong/expired/replayed OTP, login, logout/revocation, recovery, resend throttling and provider outage. Mark provider-unavailable or unsupported cases unverified rather than simulating observed behavior.

AC2 defines observable counters/outcome categories for authentication success/failure, OTP delivery failure, throttling and rollback trigger from actual configured signals. Labels/time window/thresholds require a documented operator policy; no unsupported metric or numeric SLO is invented. Logs contain request/correlation ID and bounded category only, never credentials, OTP, auth code, token, recipient address or provider payload.

AC3 requires a protected manual deployment of an exact reviewed commit with green exact-SHA CI, migration/config checks, deployment provenance and health smoke. Rollback must restore the previous authentication behavior/config without deleting identity or user data, and verify the prior login path; no automatic deployment or branch other than main is implied.

AC4 is a human release acceptance after owner reviews the same immutable live evidence bundle: disposable flow results, monitoring, exact deployed SHA, rollback result and unresolved risks. Owner acceptance is not inferred from code review or hosted CI alone.
technicalApproach: This is a release/acceptance plan around the existing Fastify server-side Cognito callback/session boundary, PostgreSQL session ownership, manual main-only deployment and documented rollback. Do not add a new auth service, change auth runtime, or enable Cognito in this specification phase.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE: no new endpoint is introduced. Operational proof uses the existing auth start/callback, `/api/session`, login/logout and health contracts only as documented in the deployment/API sources; all endpoints must retain existing Origin/CSRF and owner-derived session rules.
persistence: No schema or migration is implied. Disposable identities are isolated provider fixtures; production candidate sessions/user data are not modified for acceptance. Test evidence stores only redacted outcomes, revision identifiers and bounded timing buckets.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION / PRIVACY_PII / SECRETS / EXTERNAL_PROVIDER / ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING / AUDIT. Provider and production are separate trust boundaries; restrict configuration/deployment to approved least-privilege operators, preserve MFA/branch/environment protections, never export secrets, and prevent test users/mailboxes from accessing candidate data. Authentication telemetry is minimized; owner accepts risk only after redacted exact-SHA evidence review.
observability: Before rollout identify existing source for auth request counts/errors, provider delivery/throttle outcomes, deployment revision and health. For each missing signal mark unavailable and block AC2 rather than adding speculative telemetry. Define owner, observation window, alert route and rollback trigger in the release runbook without logging per-user identifiers or authentication material.
manualExternalGates: EXTERNAL_PROVIDER: isolated Cognito/SES pool and disposable mailbox acceptance. LIVE_HOST: protected exact-main deployment/provenance, smoke and rollback verification. OWNER_DECISION: explicit go/no-go after reviewing a single revision-bound evidence bundle. No live deployment or account change occurs in Phase 3.25.
implementationChecklist: Confirm CS-90 through CS-93 implementations, owner approvals and external identity settings; keep existing login path available.
Prepare redacted disposable-account matrix for positive/negative OTP, recovery, throttling, outage, login and revocation.
Inventory actual auth telemetry and define only supported signals, thresholds, observation window, alert owner and abort criteria.
Validate the manual main-only deployment, exact SHA CI/provenance, preflight, health checks and non-destructive rollback instructions.
In a separately authorized release, run disposable and production-smoke acceptance; verify exact deployed SHA and old-path rollback without touching owner/candidate data.
Have Security, Infrastructure, QA and owner review one immutable evidence revision; record acceptance or explicit residual risks.
risksRecovery: Missing email or failed rollback can prevent account access. Keep the previously supported login path and documented previous revision/config available; abort rollout on unexpected authentication errors, delivery/throttle spike or missing provenance, then execute the established rollback and re-run health/session checks. Never restore by deleting users or resetting production data.
definitionOfDone: Implementation DoD: disposable-flow matrix, privacy-safe monitoring/runbook, manual deployment provenance and tested rollback procedure are complete and reviewed. Release DoD: exact deployed SHA passes hosted and live smoke gates; disposable email OTP/recovery/throttle/outage results are redacted and complete; rollback is observed to restore prior auth path; owner accepts the same evidence revision. Hosted and production evidence are future gates, not claimed by specification approval.

problem: The existing account form supports local email/password but does not expose a complete provider-hosted signup/OTP state machine. Current Cognito start/callback support is optional and server-exchanged; provider OTP UI/state acceptance and design coverage are not proven.
value: Give a candidate understandable, keyboard-accessible email verification and recovery states while keeping identity proof with Cognito and the authenticated session owned by CareerScope.
functionalRequirements: Actor is an unauthenticated candidate. Signup/verification is email-first per `docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-02.md#CS-90..CS-94`; phone OTP is not included. A successful provider verification must still pass through the server callback and create only the existing opaque CareerScope session; browser UI never handles/persists provider access or refresh tokens.

The approved composite reference `design/canonical/auth/careerscope-auth-account-recovery-verification-system.png` depicts desktop/mobile create-account, email verification, success, expired-link/error, forgot-password and reset-password states. For this ticket, implement only approved provider-supported email signup/verification states after CS-90/91 contract and owner configuration are accepted; do not treat password-reset artwork as proof the provider flow is configured.

Existing application routes are GET `/api/auth/cognito/start` and GET `/api/auth/cognito/callback`; provider-hosted OTP/resend is not a CareerScope-owned endpoint in the current API. Do not invent a resend API, simulate OTP acceptance, or claim signup/verification UI is implemented. Callback errors must produce bounded non-sensitive state; no token, code, OTP or provider response body is rendered.

Use explicit idle, submitting, verification-pending, resend-wait (only if a provider-supported action actually returns a retry window), invalid/expired, unavailable, success and signed-out states. Provider outage remains a DESIGN_GAP until an approved state/reference specifies copy and recovery action; never imply resend/lockout/recovery behavior unsupported by the actual provider contract.

AC4 reaches the current authenticated workspace only after the server callback establishes the opaque application cookie and session endpoint confirms it; external/provider redirects alone never count as authenticated success.
technicalApproach: Route composition remains in Next.js App Router using the existing account/auth surface and API client. Fastify `/api/auth/cognito/start` and `/api/auth/cognito/callback` remain the authorization-code boundary. Cognito-hosted UI owns provider OTP entry and resend; CareerScope renders only states returned by its server redirect/session contract. No runtime change is made in Phase 3.25.
apiContract: EXISTING_CONTRACT: GET `/api/auth/cognito/start` initiates the configured server-side authorization-code flow; GET `/api/auth/cognito/callback` validates callback state/exchanges provider response and redirects to the application; GET `/api/session` reports application session state. Exact enablement and issuer/client/callback configuration are external gates. There is no current CareerScope resend endpoint; resend is available only if the actual hosted provider page exposes it under approved policy. Never accept client-provided owner identity or provider tokens as app session.
persistence: No frontend persistence of OTPs, provider access/refresh tokens, authorization codes or session identifiers in localStorage/sessionStorage. Application auth remains an opaque HttpOnly cookie; provider exchange/session persistence is server-side. Do not add auth-state database schema in this ticket without a separate approved contract.
accessibility: All email and password inputs require persistent programmatic labels; inline validation must be associated with fields and focus first invalid field on submit. Status/error transitions use a polite/assertive live region according to urgency, announce verification progress without speaking OTP/token values, preserve visible focus through redirects, and provide keyboard-operable resend only when an approved hosted control exists. Honor reduced motion and 200% zoom/reflow; manual NVDA/VoiceOver remains required future evidence.
responsive: Match the supplied desktop and mobile compositions; verify 320/390/768/1024/1440px with no horizontal overflow, controls reachable at touch size and long localized/provider text wrapping. No locale beyond owner-approved English behavior is assumed.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION / PRIVACY_PII / SECRETS / EXTERNAL_PROVIDER / ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING. Browser is untrusted; Cognito is external identity provider; Fastify callback is the trust boundary and app session issuer. Do not expose provider tokens, OTP, auth code, raw claims or email address beyond necessary masked UI; do not infer identity from client query fields. Preserve state/PKCE, Origin/CSRF and secure-cookie rules from the existing contract. Provider errors must be generic/non-enumerating; no persistent browser storage for credentials. Rate limiting/lockout is provider policy unless an existing app contract states otherwise.
observability: Only record redacted bounded state category and correlation ID; never log email, OTP, authorization code, token, full callback URL/query or provider body. Provider-disabled, timeout, invalid-state and rejected-identity outcomes must render distinct safe states only when the server contract exposes them.
manualExternalGates: OWNER/EXTERNAL: CS-90 user-pool/client/callback and email verification settings must be approved/configured before a real OTP path can be accepted. HUMAN DESIGN: approval is needed for provider-outage/retry state absent from both cited reference boards. HUMAN ACCESSIBILITY: NVDA or VoiceOver smoke review after implementation. Current design imagery and source decision do not prove hosted Cognito acceptance.
implementationChecklist: Confirm CS-90/91 contract and provider enablement; keep local-password path behavior unchanged as fallback.
Map current auth route and callback response/session states to exact UI states without adding provider operations.
Apply supplied desktop/mobile reference to only the supported email signup and verification states; obtain an outage-state design before implementing that unresolved presentation.
Implement labeled form/error/status/focus behavior and privacy-safe redirects; do not store OTP/token/code in browser state.
Add component/API mock tests for success, invalid/expired state, provider-disabled and unavailable server responses; add Chromium/Firefox/WebKit keyboard and responsive browser cases.
Complete axe checks and manual screen-reader/design review; use disposable Cognito acceptance only after external configuration is authorized.
Document and verify current exact SHA evidence; leave hosted/provider gates open until actually executed.
risksRecovery: A frontend success state without a server-created session can mislead the candidate; provider outage copy can imply unsafe retries; leaking callback query data can disclose credentials. Fail closed to signed-out state, clear transient state, preserve local auth as a separate existing option, and restore the last reviewed UI revision if callback/session acceptance regresses.
definitionOfDone: Implementation DoD: approved email-first session/provider contract; exact supported state matrix; design review of supplied auth references plus approved outage state; no token/code/OTP persistence/rendering; labeled keyboard flow and announcements; component/API and Chromium/Firefox/WebKit tests pass; accessibility automation and human screen-reader acceptance recorded; successful callback is confirmed by GET `/api/session` and workspace navigation; errors remain signed out. Release DoD additionally requires disposable hosted Cognito OTP acceptance and exact-SHA CI. No provider setup or product implementation is claimed by this specification.

problem: There is no verified sender/SES/Cognito template evidence. The approved owner record only targets a verified CareerScope domain identity; it does not choose a concrete From/Reply-To address, locale set, visual treatment, expiry duration, DNS records or SES production-access state.
value: Provide trustworthy, abuse-resistant email verification messages only after sender ownership, template correctness, delivery controls and real disposable-account delivery are evidenced.
functionalRequirements: Owner decision provenance: `docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-02.md#CS-90..CS-94` approves a verified CareerScope domain identity as the sender target; exact From/Reply-To addresses, supported locales and template visual acceptance remain undecided. Do not guess addresses, translate copy, claim a verified sender or copy illustrative design content.

For the current email-code flow, the Cognito verification template must contain the provider's required `{####}` code placeholder and state only the exact expiry duration configured for the approved pool. The duration is unresolved until the pool configuration is approved; do not hard-code a guessed number. Do not use a verification link template in place of email OTP without an explicit product decision.

Template body/subject may contain only approved product name, concise security guidance, the required code placeholder, configured expiry, and owner-approved support route. Do not include passwords, access/refresh tokens, authorization codes, raw profile fields, candidate data or unnecessary recipient identifiers. Ensure HTML and text variants have equivalent meaning and no remote scripts/assets.

Record the exact Cognito email-sending mode, SES identity/region, DKIM status, sandbox/production status, daily/rate quotas, bounce/complaint/suppression handling, relevant DNS record names/status (never secret values), and operational owner. Use observed provider configuration, not documentation-only assumptions.

A real verification message may be tested only with an isolated disposable Cognito account and a non-personal mailbox controlled for acceptance. Enter the OTP interactively; repository/CI evidence may store only redacted outcome, template/config revision, delivery status and timing bucket—never the OTP, recipient address, mailbox content or tokens.
nonFunctionalRequirements: Template text/HTML must stay within Cognito's current documented message-size limit, preserve required placeholders for selected message type, render without external network assets and remain readable with plain-text fallback. Provider quotas and expiry are account/config evidence, not assumed SLOs.
technicalApproach: Use Cognito user-pool message-template configuration with the approved SES sending identity; do not build a separate email microservice or direct-send OTP path. AWS documents `{####}` for code templates and configurable From/Reply-To; account/domain verification and SES sandbox status must be checked in the actual selected region. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pool-settings-message-customizations.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/user-pool-email.html.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE: CS-92 configures provider messages; it adds no application HTTP endpoint. Cognito-managed signup/verification operations remain provider contracts governed by CS-90/CS-91.
persistence: No CareerScope database schema or user-data persistence change. Store only nonsensitive template source and redacted configuration/run evidence. AWS sender secrets, mailbox access and raw messages stay outside Git and test artifacts.
accessibility: Email content must be understandable in text-only clients, use a descriptive subject and readable code/expiry instructions, avoid color-only meaning, and keep the one-time code easy to select/read. Manual assistive-technology review is required for any HTML email styling; no visual acceptance is claimed here.
responsive: Verify the plain-text and HTML message remain readable without horizontal scrolling at narrow mobile widths and at desktop widths; do not embed fixed-width content or remote assets.
browsers: NOT_APPLICABLE to provider configuration itself; real-message content can be inspected in supported desktop/mobile email clients only through a disposable mailbox. Browser QA is not a substitute for actual delivery.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: authentication emails and their templates are private and must never be indexed or added to a public sitemap.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: PRIVACY_PII / SECRETS / EXTERNAL_PROVIDER / ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING / DATA_RETENTION. Restrict AWS and DNS changes to explicitly authorized least-privilege operators; never put OTPs, recipient email, raw message, mailbox credentials, access keys, provider tokens or DNS verification secrets in repository evidence. A test message must not be sent to a real candidate or owner account. Preserve Cognito non-enumeration and resend throttles; treat bounce/complaint signals as private operational data with retention/redaction limits.
observability: Record privacy-safe send outcome categories, provider rejection/throttle, bounce/complaint/suppression counts and delivery-latency buckets only where the configured provider provides them. Define the actual alert/owner response path; never log recipient address, OTP, token, full message or mailbox content. If bounce/complaint events are not configured, disclose the gap and keep production acceptance blocked.
manualExternalGates: OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED: exact From/Reply-To, brand/copy approval, supported locale list, expiry wording/duration and support destination. EXTERNAL_GATE: verified SES domain identity and DKIM/DNS status in ap-south-1, Cognito sender configuration, SES sandbox removal/production access and actual quota/bounce/complaint handling. No DNS or AWS changes occur in Phase 3.25; record only redacted evidence.
implementationChecklist: Obtain exact owner From/Reply-To, brand/copy, locale, expiry and support decisions; do not infer them from the sender-domain target.
Inspect approved Cognito/SES config in the selected region and record sending mode, verified identity/DKIM, sandbox/production and current quotas without secrets.
Create code-based verification and authentication templates that use the required `{####}` placeholder and match the approved expiry; omit unnecessary personal data and all credentials/tokens.
Define and test bounce/complaint/suppression handling and the accountable alert/response path using a safe provider test mechanism.
Run static template/placeholder/privacy checks, text/HTML equivalence and narrow-screen readability checks.
Send one real message only to an isolated disposable user/mailbox; verify delivery and successful code entry without retaining OTP, address or message contents.
Obtain Product/Security/QA approval and retain redacted configuration/evidence; production sending remains gated on SES access and DNS verification.
risksRecovery: Wrong sender identity or incomplete DNS may cause non-delivery, phishing suspicion or provider rejection. Incorrect expiry wording can mislead a user; compare copy to exact pool configuration before enabling. If a sender/template change harms delivery, disable Cognito rollout or restore the last approved template/config revision; do not delete identities or rotate unrelated credentials. Bounce/complaint spikes require pausing sends per the approved operator procedure.
definitionOfDone: Implementation DoD: sender/From/Reply-To and locale/copy decisions are approved; Cognito template placeholders and expiry match selected settings; privacy/security checks pass; actual SES identity/DKIM/sandbox/quota/bounce handling are verified; a disposable-account message is delivered and code accepted with no OTP/PII in evidence; Product/Security/QA approve the same revision. Release DoD additionally requires production sender access, domain/DNS proof, current quota/monitoring and production smoke evidence. No AWS, DNS or email was changed during Phase 3.25.

problem: The existing API has an optional Cognito authorization-code start/callback path, but provider OTP signup/resend behavior, verified-email-only owner resolution, privacy-safe failure evidence and disposable-provider acceptance are not established as complete. Current code also accepts a verified phone as an alternate external identity; the approved owner decision makes phone OTP a later capability, so this path must not be treated as current-release approval.
value: Deliver the approved email-first authentication flow without creating a second owner, weakening the existing opaque-session boundary or claiming provider acceptance from local mocks.
functionalRequirements: Current-release scope is email identifier and Cognito-hosted email signup/verification/login. Phone is optional contact only; phone OTP is a later capability under `docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-02.md#CS-90..CS-94` and is excluded here. Do not add a CareerScope OTP or resend endpoint: Cognito-hosted UI owns the OTP entry/resend surface unless a separately approved architecture changes that boundary.

Use the existing `GET /api/auth/cognito/start` and `/api/auth/cognito/callback` contract only while CS-90 approves the exact pool/client/callback configuration. The server starts authorization-code + PKCE using the configured issuer, client and callback, then exchanges the returned code server-to-server and derives identity from verified Cognito profile claims; do not place OTP values, access/refresh tokens or provider secrets in a CareerScope URL, browser storage, logs or repository artifacts.

Create/resolve exactly one CareerScope owner by verified normalized email and provider subject under the approved account-linking rule. Missing, unverified, phone-only, duplicate or conflicting identity fails closed without creating or transferring ownership. Do not export the existing Argon2 password hash.

After accepted identity, issue only the existing opaque CareerScope application session cookie with the existing `HttpOnly`, `Secure` in HTTPS, `SameSite=Strict`, `/api` scope and expiry semantics. `POST /api/logout` revokes the application session and clears its cookie; do not claim Cognito global sign-out unless separately approved and implemented.

The provider-hosted email OTP resend limit and verification expiry/reuse policy are defined by the approved Cognito pool settings. The application start/callback rate limits remain distinct controls; do not invent provider quotas or describe the current `/api/auth/cognito/start` limiter as OTP resend throttling.

Return only bounded, non-enumerating error categories. Provider outage, invalid/expired/replayed callback state, unverified email, identity collision and disabled Cognito must not issue a session; clear transient state/verifier cookies on callback failure. Keep the current Argon2/session path available while Cognito is disabled or rolled back.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: AUTH_IDENTITY / THIRD_PARTY_INTEGRATION / API_CONTRACT / DATA_MODEL. `apps/api/src/app.ts` composes current `/api/auth/cognito/start`, `/api/auth/cognito/callback`, `/api/session`, `/api/logout` and Argon2 `/api/login`; `packages/core/src/auth.ts` owns application sessions and external identity linking. Preserve these module boundaries; do not add runtime code or schema in this specification phase.
apiContract: EXISTING_CONTRACT: `GET /api/auth/cognito/start` redirects to the configured issuer and sets short-lived HttpOnly state/verifier cookies; `GET /api/auth/cognito/callback` validates the returned code/state, exchanges code server-side, reads provider profile, resolves a verified identity, and redirects with the local opaque session cookie on success; `GET /api/session` reports the application session; `POST /api/logout` revokes the local session. OpenAPI is `apps/api/src/openapi.ts`. `POST /api/register` remains the separate Argon2 route and may be disabled; it is not Cognito OTP signup.

No CareerScope OTP-verification or resend endpoint currently exists or is approved. OTP entry, email verification and resend remain the Cognito-hosted user-pool contract. If an approved provider setup requires an app-owned endpoint, stop for a separately reviewed contract; do not infer one.

Callback must accept only configured redirect URI/issuer and a valid one-time authorization code bound to the short-lived state/verifier; return stable bounded failure categories without echoing provider values. Exact pool/client allowlists and error semantics depend on CS-90 approval and must be marked unresolved until supplied.
persistence: Reuse the current PostgreSQL owner/session/provider-identity persistence implemented by `packages/core/src/auth.ts` and `database.ts`; do not introduce a new OTP table because Cognito owns OTPs. Require unique owner linkage for normalized verified email/provider subject according to the approved migration contract. No owner/profile/application data changes on failed or ambiguous identity; migration/backfill and rollback need separate disposable-Postgres tests before release.
accessibility: CareerScope does not implement the Cognito-hosted OTP controls in this ticket. Hosted-page keyboard, labels, focus/error announcements, contrast, zoom/reflow and manual NVDA/VoiceOver checks remain a provider acceptance gate; the local sign-in link must keep an accessible name and visible focus under its separate UI ticket.
responsive: No new CareerScope layout is introduced. Browser acceptance must confirm the redirect and return path works from mobile, tablet and desktop without a blank/error loop; provider-hosted page reflow is externally validated at 320/390/768/1024/1440 widths when supported.
browsers: Mocked application callback tests target Chromium-independent API integration; browser acceptance for the local entry and provider redirect/return must cover Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Real provider OTP acceptance is a separate external gate, not inferred from the browser suite.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: authentication and callback surfaces are private and must remain non-indexable; no identity or callback parameters may enter public metadata or sitemap output.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION / PRIVACY_PII / SECRETS / ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING / AUDIT / DATA_RETENTION. Trust boundaries are browser, CareerScope API/session store, Cognito hosted UI, provider token endpoint and PostgreSQL. Accept verified email and subject only; reject phone-only identity for this scope. Enforce configured redirect allowlists, state/PKCE checks, existing Origin/CSRF behavior for state-changing app routes, session rotation/revocation, account non-enumeration, per-IP/application rate limits and owner-scoped data access. Never log OTP, password, authorization code, state/verifier, tokens, full callback URL, raw provider body or email/phone; redacted category and request correlation only.
observability: Emit privacy-safe counters for start/callback outcome category, throttled requests, provider timeout/unavailability, identity-link conflict and session creation/revocation. Correlate by request ID only; never log OTP, email, phone, callback query, state/verifier, authorization code, access/refresh token or provider response body. Do not claim live dashboards/alerts until measured.
manualExternalGates: HARD DEPENDENCY: CS-90 owner/security approval of user-pool/client/MFA/callback settings and feature-flag/rollback design. EXTERNAL_PROVIDER: disposable Cognito pool/client with approved ap-south-1 configuration, email sender/domain verification, actual hosted email OTP/signup/resend and callback acceptance. No production pool, SMS approval or real owner-account migration is implied; owner account is never used as a test fixture.
implementationChecklist: Close CS-90 pool/client/callback/MFA and rollback approval before enabling the route.
Compare current API callback identity handling with the verified-email-only owner decision; reject unverified, phone-only, duplicate and conflicting identities before session creation.
Add deterministic integration coverage for start state/PKCE cookies, valid/invalid callback, provider outage, session issuance/revocation and unchanged Argon2 fallback.
Add privacy assertions over URL, browser storage, application logs and repository/publication artifacts using synthetic sentinels.
Run disposable Cognito email signup/OTP/resend/login/logout and negative cases; capture redacted provider evidence only.
Run cross-owner authorization, Origin/CSRF, cookie and session-revocation tests plus Chromium/Firefox/WebKit auth redirect coverage.
Obtain Security and QA review; document provider-specific manual gates and keep Cognito disabled until exact-SHA canary acceptance.
risksRecovery: Phone-only identity acceptance conflicts with the recorded email-first release boundary and could create or link the wrong owner; fail closed. A provider timeout or partial callback must clear transient cookies and issue no app session. Keep the Argon2 path usable until verified disposable-account E2E, monitoring, owner continuity, backup and rollback gates pass. Never retry a real owner migration from a partially applied state.
definitionOfDone: Implementation DoD: provider-hosted email signup/verification/resend and login work against the approved CS-90 config; verified normalized email resolves one owner; local session cookies/revocation, Origin/CSRF and owner isolation remain intact; phone-only identity is rejected for current release; all negative/privacy/browser tests pass and no OTP/token/PII leaks. Release DoD separately requires disposable Cognito acceptance, protected exact-SHA canary, monitoring, owner continuity and rollback evidence. Phase 3.25 specifies these gates only and performs none of them.

problem: The source records an identity-authority migration handoff. The 2026-10-02 owner decision already approves important architecture values; do not reopen them or imply Cognito is deployed. Current source still has Argon2id credentials and opaque server-side sessions, and the separate email/provider, frontend and live rollout gates remain distinct tickets.
value: Make the Cognito migration design explicit enough to protect account uniqueness, existing candidate data, browser-session ownership and rollback before any identity cutover.
functionalRequirements: Propagate the owner-approved values from `docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-02.md`: Cognito region `ap-south-1`; normalized/case-insensitive verified email as the primary account identifier; Cognito as hosted identity authority while CareerScope retains its opaque application session after server-side verification/exchange; browser storage never retains Cognito access/refresh tokens; target custom domain `auth.careerscope.tech` after DNS/certificate readiness; existing owner linked once by verified normalized email; existing Argon2 password hashes are never exported; rollout is feature-flagged/canary with the current Argon2/session path available for rollback until disposable-account E2E, monitoring and owner-account continuity pass. These are approved design decisions, not proof of provider configuration or activation.

The same owner-decision record classifies phone number as optional contact initially and phone OTP login as a later capability. Preserve that release boundary unless a newer explicit owner decision is recorded; CS-91's current frozen criteria specify email OTP. Do not infer SMS approval or mobile OTP delivery from email OTP support.

AC1 is partly resolved by the approved region, primary identifier and custom-domain target above. The exact user-pool/client settings, callback/logout allowlists, verification/MFA policy, and operator evidence of actual AWS configuration must be documented without secrets before the design gate can close. The custom domain remains conditional on DNS/certificate readiness.

AC2 flow must specify signup initiation, email OTP verification/resend, login, server callback validation, one-time code/token exchange, CareerScope opaque session issuance/rotation/revocation/logout, recovery behavior from CS-44, rate limits/abuse controls, Cognito outage behavior and rollback to the pre-existing Argon2/session flow. Provider tokens stay server-side and are discarded/redacted after identity verification; do not invent Cognito grants/endpoints beyond official configuration and the existing application contract.

AC3 migration is one-to-one by normalized verified email with a preflight uniqueness/conflict report; create no second owner or duplicate profile, and never transfer local password hashes to Cognito. The user data remains in CareerScope Postgres, linked only after an unambiguous identity match; conflicting/missing/unverified email causes a fail-closed manual resolution, not guessed account merge. Migration execution and backup evidence are separate operational acceptance.

AC4 threat-model review covers browser/provider/API trust boundaries, code/state/nonce/PKCE verification, CSRF/Origin, redirect allowlists, replay, session fixation, account enumeration, OTP abuse, rate limits, email/SMS delivery abuse, provider outage, identity collision, token leakage, retention/deletion and rollback/cutover failure. Security and System Designer must review the same immutable design revision before CS-91 or related implementation may proceed; keep blocked=true metadata until then and preserve the canonical workflow stage.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: AUTH_IDENTITY / THIRD_PARTY_INTEGRATION / API_CONTRACT / DATA_MODEL. Future Cognito verification is server-to-server; the application issues its existing opaque cookie session and never exposes provider tokens to the browser. apiContract: No new HTTP endpoint is approved by CS-90. Mark any not-yet-approved callback route as PLANNED, not implemented.
persistence: Preserve existing application user/profile ownership and data. The future identity map must be unique for normalized verified email and external subject, maintain one CareerScope owner, use a reviewed migration/rollback plan, and leave user content in PostgreSQL. Any schema/key/index or retention change requires a separately reviewed migration; do not place OTPs, tokens or passwords in repository state.
accessibility: Architecture-only ticket: no rendered form is implemented here. Future UI tickets must use the approved auth references, accessible OTP labels/errors/status announcements, keyboard/focus/reflow behavior, and manual screen-reader validation.
browsers: NOT_APPLICABLE to this architecture document; future callback/session UI acceptance belongs to CS-91 and the auth-front-end ticket with Chromium, Firefox and WebKit coverage.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: authentication and callback routes are private/non-indexable and must not expose identity data in metadata or sitemap output.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION / PRIVACY_PII / SECRETS / ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING / DATA_RETENTION. Trust boundaries are user agent, CareerScope API/session store, Cognito, email/SMS delivery provider and existing Postgres. Verify the provider response server-side; the application remains owner of app sessions and authorization. Allow OAuth authorization code and state only in the required authorization/callback query transport; allow state only in its bounded short-lived HttpOnly transient cookie and the PKCE verifier only in its bounded short-lived HttpOnly transient cookie. Clear both cookies on success and every callback failure, then redirect to a clean application URL. Do not persist these values durably, expose them through logs, analytics, fixtures, Git, evidence or browser storage. OTPs and Cognito access/refresh tokens are never permitted in URLs or browser storage. Never log passwords, verifier/nonce secrets or Cognito tokens; redact callback query values and raw provider errors. Restrict migration scope to the single owner record and preserve data; do not export password hashes or merge on unverified identifiers.
observability: The architecture must name privacy-safe metrics for auth success/failure category, OTP send/verification throttling, provider latency/errors, session exchange/revocation and migration conflicts, with correlation IDs but no email, phone, OTP, token, authorization code, or raw callback URL. Define alerts and a safe rollback signal; live observability remains future evidence.
manualExternalGates: OWNER_DECISION / EXTERNAL_GATE: use approved 2026-10-02 architecture values as the baseline. Phone OTP is already classified as a later capability in that record and is not an unresolved CS-90 decision; CS-91's current frozen criteria specify email OTP. problem: The repository has a shared route/permission and transactional UX contract, but no single ticket-specific matrix currently proves how route surface, authenticated principal, server permission, release state, feature flag, denial behavior and high-risk mutation confirmation compose. UI visibility must not become authorization, and planned contracts must not be mistaken for implemented endpoints.
value: Give implementation and reviewers one fail-closed contract for authorization boundaries and transactional interactions, reducing privilege-escalation, duplicate-command, stale-revision and unsafe-release risk without broadening any product surface.
functionalRequirements: Maintain a machine-readable route/role/release/flag matrix from authoritative route registrations and approved design contracts. Every entry names surface, authentication requirement, server permission, release/feature gate and safe unauthorized/unavailable behavior; an omitted route remains absent rather than implicitly public.

Server/API authorization derives the principal and resource owner from the authenticated session and persisted data. Client-selected owner IDs, roles, permissions, flags, consent, route visibility and browser storage never grant access; direct unauthorized requests are denied before protected reads or writes.

For high-risk mutations, the owning domain contract must require explicit confirmation and, where specified, reason capture, idempotency/replay protection, revision or lease/fencing checks, and an immutable safe audit event. CS-104 does not invent a mutation endpoint or generic admin database operation.

Positive, unauthenticated, unauthorized, malformed, stale/conflicting, duplicate, unavailable and provider/queue failure fixtures map to each existing or explicitly planned contract. UI pending/disabled/denied state is a presentation of server result, never a security control.

Release or feature metadata alone cannot activate a surface. Activation requires the declared route, permission, domain contract, security/privacy, accessibility, hosted/release and rollback evidence; current ticket state remains BACKLOG/RELEASE and no runtime activation occurs in Phase 3.25.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE / API_CONTRACT / ASYNC_SYSTEM. Keep route composition in the canonical Next.js/Fastify modules and use existing session, CSRF/origin, idempotency, revision, outbox, lease and fencing abstractions where their domain contracts already exist. This ticket defines the contract and matrix; it does not add a new service, route, database model or queue.

SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION, AUTHORIZATION, ADMIN_PRIVILEGE, INPUT_VALIDATION, ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING and AUDIT. Treat the browser as untrusted and enforce all boundaries on the server before repository access; fail closed when a permission, release, revision or capability result is missing, stale or unavailable.
apiContract: Use EXISTING_CONTRACT entries only where they are present in apps/api/src/app.ts and the documented API surface. For a future child capability, specify PLANNED_CONTRACT separately with method, route, actor, auth, authorization, request validation, response allowlist, stable errors and ownership before registration; do not invent paths in CS-104.

Every mutating contract preserves canonical CSRF/origin protections, stable 400/401/403/404/409/429/5xx semantics as applicable, idempotency or revision behavior where required, and no protected read on denial. UI route visibility and feature metadata are not authorization evidence.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE for new persistence in CS-104. Existing owner-scoped entities, revisions, outbox commands, leases and audit records remain authoritative. Any child migration must define constraints, uniqueness, retention, rollback and recovery in its own ticket before implementation.
accessibility: Contract-driven pending, disabled, denied, expired, conflict and failure states must have semantic status/error associations, keyboard-operable confirmation controls, visible focus, focus restoration after dialogs, and non-color-only explanation. Automated axe/browser evidence and a separate NVDA/VoiceOver judgment remain future gates; inaccessible UI cannot be excused by a server denial.
responsive: Shared confirmation/error/pending patterns must remain usable at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS pixels with no unintended overflow, clipped focus or inaccessible touch targets. This shared contract does not create a new visual page; feature-specific layouts remain owned by their tickets.
browsers: Future component/browser verification covers Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with synthetic principals and contract fixtures. Missing browser or contract evidence is NOT_RUN, never PASS.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE for this internal contract; authenticated/private surfaces remain noindex and no route matrix entry may expose permission, operational or user data through metadata.
securityPrivacy: Trust boundary: client route, method, IDs, headers, roles, flags, revisions, reason text and consent claims are untrusted. The session establishes the principal; repository queries enforce ownership and least privilege. Admin privilege is an allowlisted domain capability, not generic database access.

Sensitive fields include sessions, CSRF values, provider tokens, resumes, contact data, audit details and infrastructure metadata. Redact them from logs, error bodies, fixtures, screenshots and telemetry. Rate-limit authentication and high-risk mutations according to existing contracts; audit actor, action, target, reason, correlation ID and safe result without secrets or raw PII.

Abuse cases include direct-route privilege escalation, owner-ID substitution, stale-session replay, duplicate mutation, stale revision overwrite, forged confirmation/reason, malformed input, provider timeout and queue/DLQ failure. Each owning contract must return a safe error and preserve data/event invariants.
observability: Use existing request/correlation IDs and safe outcome categories for allow, deny, conflict, duplicate, retry, timeout and unavailable states. Record audit events only for approved mutations; never log credentials, tokens, raw resumes, request bodies or fabricated success metrics.
visualRegression: DESIGN_NOT_APPLICABLE for the shared contract itself. Feature tickets that render confirmation, denial or transactional states must bind their own approved screen/state reference and visual evidence; no screenshot is treated as an authorization or data contract.
manualExternalGates: Security and release reviewers must approve the route/role/release/flag matrix and high-risk mutation contract before activation. Hosted exact-SHA CI, live authorization/rollback evidence and human accessibility review remain future gates where required; no operator or production action is performed by this specification.
risksRecovery: Primary risks are UI-only authorization, overbroad admin capability, duplicate or stale mutation, and partial async effects. On a denied/unknown/stale result, perform no protected read/write and render the contract-defined safe state. On a conflict, preserve the current revision and require refresh/review; on an outbox/worker failure, retain at-least-once/idempotent/fenced semantics. Rollback removes the contract consumer or flag, not historical audit/data.
definitionOfDone: Specification DoD: route matrix fields and denial semantics are explicit; existing versus planned contracts are distinguished; ownership, CSRF/origin, idempotency/revision/fencing, audit/redaction, failure states, accessibility/responsive/browser gates and release boundary are ticket-specific; no runtime/API/schema implementation is claimed.

Future implementation DoD: every matrix entry has server tests for positive/denial/malformed/failure paths; high-risk mutations have confirmation/reason/idempotency/concurrency/audit evidence; UI states are keyboard/axe/browser verified; hosted exact-SHA, security, rollback and human accessibility evidence are recorded before RELEASE activation.

securityPrivacy: Trust boundary: browser and all client-selected IDs, roles, permissions, flags and consent claims are untrusted; the session and API derive the principal and every capability. Resource owners vary by child domain; candidate data remains candidate-owned, and admin access is least-privilege operational access, not ownership transfer.

The shell receives only a server-authorized navigation/view model and has no direct database, host, provider or secret-manager access. Reject or safely deny unauthenticated, unauthorized, expired/revoked session, stale capability, malformed state and failed permission resolution before any child data read. Never use a UI flag or route visibility as authorization.

Operational logs/telemetry may contain security-sensitive infrastructure details and PII. Require child APIs to redact passwords, secrets, access/refresh tokens, cookies, authorization headers, resume contents, full email/phone, raw request bodies and unnecessary identifiers before returning or logging data. Do not expose raw credentials, arbitrary shell/database controls, or unbounded cross-candidate reads.

Potential abuse includes privilege escalation by direct URL/API call, cross-role access, stale-session replay, query/filter injection, log/metric cardinality abuse, secret enumeration and use of the shell to trigger destructive operations. The shell defines no mutation/query endpoint; child tickets must specify rate limits, audit events, reason capture and confirmation where their operation risk requires them.
observability: The shell adds no operational telemetry or audit record. Future child APIs expose only contract-defined safe status categories and request correlation IDs; they must distinguish success, empty, stale, denied, unavailable and error without logging response payloads or secrets. Never substitute generated metrics for missing telemetry.
visualRegression: DESIGN_PARTIAL / NON_BLOCKING for specification: the design index assigns a full 16-panel production-operations board to CS-103 and identifies selected mobile examples, but does not map a dedicated shell-only crop, exact shell state or mobile navigation frame. This is sufficient to specify a FUTURE reusable shell boundary, not sufficient to claim exact shell parity. UX must select the crop/state, approve mobile behavior, dynamic masks and numeric tolerance before visual implementation acceptance; no illustrated operational values may be used as fixtures or expected production values.
manualExternalGates: MANUAL_PRODUCT / UX: approve the production-operations shell-only crop, mobile navigation, and predeclared visual comparison tolerance before implementation acceptance. SECURITY / RELEASE GATE: CS-104 must establish route, admin role, release/feature-flag and safe-denial semantics; each child operational ticket must establish its API, data allowlist, authorization, audit and retention contract before the shell exposes it. MANUAL_ACCESSIBILITY: a qualified human completes the NVDA or VoiceOver smoke test on the authorized future build. No operator/host action is performed by this specification.
risksRecovery: Primary risks are treating the admin shell as authorization, rendering invented/overbroad telemetry, or leaking secrets/PII through logs and shell metadata. Default to no route/data and fail closed on missing/stale permission. On a future permission-loss or fetch error, discard sensitive view state and return to the contract-defined denial/unavailable screen. Rollback removes shell presentation only; it must not alter host, queue, backup, provider or candidate data.
definitionOfDone: Specification DoD: shell-only FUTURE scope; child and cross-cutting ownership; canonical board and partial-design/non-blocking rationale; no invented route/API/schema; server-side permission, redaction and no-fake-telemetry rules; pending/empty/error/denial/expiry behavior; accessibility/responsive/browser requirements; all exact AC bindings; no runtime implementation claim.

Future implementation/release DoD: CS-104 route/role/release contract and each exposed child API/data/security contract are approved; default hidden remains enforced; direct unauthorized requests cause zero protected reads; only redacted contract-backed state renders; all actions are owned and audited by child APIs; desktop/mobile visual and browser/a11y checks pass; human screen-reader validation and exact-SHA release gate evidence are recorded.

problem: The approved recruiter board describes a FUTURE workspace, but the current repository does not provide a recruiter product route, recruiter authorization/session contract, candidate-consent persistence contract, or recruiter API. The ticket is a reusable shell boundary; it must not treat board data or proposed `stage_9_enabled` metadata as proof that recruiter functionality is active.
value: Keep a future recruiter experience visually and architecturally composable while preventing shell/navigation visibility from becoming authorization or disclosing candidate data before server-enforced recruiter permissions and current candidate consent exist.
functionalRequirements: CS-102 owns only a reusable recruiter workspace frame/navigation boundary. It does not assign a standalone URL; child screens remain owned by CS-177–CS-192, and their routes/actions are not inferred from image labels.

The recruiter surface remains FUTURE and hidden/unavailable under the current product configuration. The registry's proposed `stage_9_enabled` value is planning metadata, not an existing runtime feature flag or authorization decision.

In any separately authorized future rendering, the shell receives only a server-derived recruiter principal, permission result, and candidate-visibility result from approved contracts. If recruiter authentication, candidate consent, permission, or scope is absent, unknown, expired, or withdrawn, render no candidate-specific content and do not cache it; use the finalized safe denial/unavailable behavior from the route-permission contract.

Never accept a recruiter identity, candidate owner ID, consent state, role, or permission from a client-selected value as authority. Navigation hiding is not access control; each child API must enforce authorization independently.

The shell does not implement candidate search, match scoring, profile/resume/contact access, job posting, outreach, messaging, pipeline mutation, interview scheduling, analytics, company management or settings. These are separate child tickets and contracts.

All board names, counts, match values, candidate identities, messages, company values and statuses are illustrative. Use only contract-backed data or an explicit empty/unavailable state; unknown remains unknown.

No shell action may imply candidate consent, recruiter privilege, successful outreach, interview state, application state, or verified candidate data. Do not rank on protected traits, scrape unauthorized sources, expose secrets, or send messages from shell navigation.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE presentation boundary over the canonical Next.js authenticated layout, shared UI primitives and future recruiter child features; no route, API, provider, database entity, queue or worker is created by this ticket.

Use the existing recruiter full reference board as contextual visual authority for the shared frame only. Keep individual screen geometry and business operations with CS-177–CS-192. Route/role/release/feature-flag and server denial behavior must follow CS-104's route-permission contract before implementation; shared UI primitives follow CS-95/CS-106 where applicable.
apiContract: NOT_APPLICABLE for CS-102 itself: it defines no HTTP endpoint, request or persistence operation. Any recruiter read or mutation must be separately specified by its owning child ticket and server contract; this shell specification does not invent route paths, data shapes, consent endpoints, status codes, or candidate fields.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE: the shell stores no recruiter identity, candidate record, consent, profile, resume, contact detail, message, campaign, pipeline state or audit event. Do not persist UI-derived permissions or consent state in browser storage. Data/consent persistence and retention require an independently approved domain contract before any child implementation.
securityPrivacy: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE. SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION, AUTHORIZATION, PRIVACY_PII, ADMIN_PRIVILEGE boundary separation, AUDIT for future sensitive child actions, and DATA_RETENTION for any future candidate disclosure.

Trust boundary: browser is untrusted; API/session and consent/permission service are authoritative. Candidate remains the data owner. Recruiter reads are limited to the exact fields and purpose authorized by a current server-validated consent and role policy; shell must fail closed on missing or stale decisions. No raw resume or contact information is allowed in shell chrome, navigation metadata, logs, screenshots or telemetry.

The shell must not provide an admin/database control surface or reuse candidate permissions as recruiter permissions. Any future privileged action is a child contract, must be least-privilege, server-authorized and auditable, and must not accept client-provided owner identity.
accessibility: The shared frame must preserve semantic navigation/landmarks, a programmatic current-page state, visible keyboard focus, logical tab order, accessible names for navigation controls, Escape/focus restoration for any separately approved dialog, and non-color-only active/disabled indicators. A real NVDA or VoiceOver smoke test remains a human release gate after the shell exists; axe is not a substitute.
responsive: Use the recruiter contract's desktop board as the visual reference and preserve its information hierarchy on small viewports; do not scale the desktop board. No canonical recruiter mobile crop is identified for the shell. Before implementation acceptance, UX must approve the mobile navigation/shell state; verify 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS-pixel widths, no unintended horizontal overflow, keyboard and touch operation, and 44px-class targets where applicable.
browsers: Future browser acceptance covers Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with recorded versions and exact authorized routes/states; missing or unavailable engines are NOT_RUN, not PASS. Use synthetic candidates and consent fixtures only.
seo: NOT_APPLICABLE: recruiter workspace is authenticated and private; its future routes must be noindex and must not expose recruiter/candidate data in metadata, canonical URLs, previews or sitemaps.
observability: The shell adds no telemetry or audit events. Future sensitive reads/actions are instrumented by their owning API/domain tickets with correlation IDs and safe outcome categories only; never record candidate identifiers beyond the approved safe form, candidate content, resume/contact details, consent payloads, session material or message bodies.
visualRegression: DESIGN_PARTIAL / NON_BLOCKING for specification: `design/DESIGN-INDEX.json#recruiter` assigns the FUTURE stage and canonical full board to CS-102, while the 16 individual recruiter screens are assigned to CS-177–CS-192. The index does not identify a separately cropped shell-only state or canonical mobile shell image. This does not block specifying a reusable frame boundary, but visual implementation acceptance must wait for UX to identify the exact shell crop/state and approve mobile navigation and measurable tolerance; do not mask child-screen layout or use sample board values as production data.
manualExternalGates: MANUAL_PRODUCT / UX: before shell implementation is accepted, approve the exact recruiter-shell/navigation subset of the full board, the mobile shell state and comparison threshold. EXTERNAL/ARCHITECTURE GATE: CS-104 must establish route/role/release/flag and safe denial contracts; child tickets must define recruiter principal, consent semantics, data fields and API authorization before candidate data is visible. These are future implementation gates, not evidence that the capability is configured or active.
risksRecovery: Primary risk is treating navigation visibility or a client consent bit as authorization and rendering candidate PII to the wrong recruiter. Keep the surface unavailable until server contracts pass; on permission/consent loss, invalidate any local view and return to the approved denial state. Roll back only the shell presentation, never candidate data/consent records; no such records are introduced by CS-102.
definitionOfDone: Specification DoD: scope limited to reusable FUTURE recruiter frame; route is not invented; CS-177–CS-192 screen ownership is preserved; exact design partial/nonblocking rationale, responsive/mobile UX gate, server-side permission and consent prerequisites, API/data NOT_APPLICABLE, security/privacy, negative states, browser matrix, accessible navigation, exact AC bindings and no-runtime-work boundary are explicit.

Future implementation DoD: CS-104 authorization contract and approved recruiter/consent data contracts exist; feature remains hidden until explicit release; no candidate content appears without server-authorized current consent; child actions enforce their own server authorization; visual and responsive reviews use approved states and synthetic data; cross-browser, automated accessibility/security, human screen-reader and exact-SHA release evidence pass.

problem: CS-101 is a cross-cutting truthfulness and capability-gating boundary, not the owner of the AI Apply Assistant screen. The design index assigns that screen to CS-130 and records its route UNKNOWN; current runtime supports only the separately scoped, optional preparation-coaching elaboration. The design board is planning context, not proof that its application, resume-tailoring, cover-letter or apply controls exist.
value: Prevent the candidate UI from promising, exposing or invoking AI behavior that is not implemented, authorized and enabled, while preserving the existing deterministic preparation report and user-controlled decisions.
functionalRequirements: For the current capability, the authenticated `/preparation` surface may render the per-item `Get AI coaching` control only when the server-derived session reports `aiEnabled: true`; pending, unauthenticated, expired or false capability state renders no active AI control. Do not derive availability from design metadata, local storage or a client-selected identity.

When the candidate explicitly activates one preparation item, display only the server response for that item with the visible `AI-generated coaching` label. Render response text as escaped text, never HTML. A 503 capability-disabled response renders the explicit unavailable message; other failures remain errors and never substitute a sample answer.

No AI application assistant route, application submission, resume rewrite, cover-letter generation, arbitrary chat, scoring, ranking, eligibility, matching exclusion, ownership or application-lifecycle action is introduced by CS-101. The candidate remains the sole authority for submitting an application and opening an external destination never marks Applied.

The AI Apply Assistant reference screen remains owned by CS-130. CS-101 may specify the shared capability/truthfulness boundary only; it does not transfer screen ownership, invent a route, assign admin access or treat design-board sample values as product data. Admin model/billing/flag surfaces remain separate tickets and are not exposed by this candidate boundary.
technicalApproach: ARCHITECTURE_IMPACT: CROSS_MODULE presentation boundary over the existing Next.js session and preparation feature; no new API, route, provider, database entity or worker. Reuse the canonical session result and existing `/api/preparation/:checkId/ai-elaborate` contract. The UI control is the existing per-item opt-in component; the AI Apply Assistant page itself belongs to CS-130.
apiContract: EXISTING_CONTRACT only: `GET /api/session` supplies server-derived `aiEnabled`; `POST /api/preparation/:checkId/ai-elaborate` returns one AI-labelled text result and is owner-scoped, rate-limited, disabled unless `AI_ENABLED` and the validated free-model configuration are present, and may return the documented 400/404/429/502/503/504 failures. It accepts no application-submission, resume, contact or compensation payload. CS-101 adds no endpoint, request field, persistence or token exposure.
persistence: NOT_APPLICABLE: CS-101 creates no AI/application record and persists no prompt, completion, resume content, provider token or client-side capability state. Existing preparation state and API ownership semantics remain unchanged.
accessibility: For the existing preparation control, the enabled button must have the visible/accessibly named action, be keyboard activatable, expose pending state without duplicate requests, and announce a returned error through the existing alert semantics. A generated result retains the visible AI-generated distinction. Manual NVDA or VoiceOver review is a separate required human gate; axe alone is not a screen-reader pass.
responsive: Verify the existing preparation item and optional control at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS pixels; no horizontal overflow or inaccessible off-screen action. Do not infer a new application-assistant mobile layout from the full reference board; CS-130 owns that visual implementation.
securityPrivacy: SECURITY_IMPACT: AUTHENTICATION / AUTHORIZATION / PRIVACY_PII / EXTERNAL_PROVIDER / ABUSE_RATE_LIMITING. The browser session identifies the candidate; the server derives owner identity and validates the preparation item. Only the existing allowlisted preparation/question text and evidence fields may cross the provider boundary. Never include resume text, contact details, compensation, session/CSRF/provider tokens or raw provider responses in UI diagnostics, logs or screenshots. A disabled/unavailable provider must fail closed without rendering fabricated output or changing deterministic results.
observability: Use existing request correlation and safe outcome categories only. Never log prompt/response text, resume/profile data, cookies, CSRF values, OpenRouter credentials or raw provider bodies. No new metric, dashboard or successful live provider claim is implied by this specification.
visualRegression: DESIGN_PARTIAL / NON_BLOCKING for CS-101's cross-cutting boundary: the ordered AI integration reference names the AI Apply Assistant panel, but the canonical index assigns the screen to CS-130 and records route UNKNOWN; current AI UI is the preparation-item control, for which no exact dedicated visual reference is indexed. Do not compare the preparation panel as though it were the AI Apply Assistant screen or implement unsupported board controls. Any future CS-130 screenshot comparison must use the exact approved screen subset and synthetic data, record 1440px desktop and UX-approved mobile viewport, Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, reference hash, dynamic masks and an owner-approved numeric acceptance threshold before execution. This is a disclosed visual gate, not a current pixel-parity claim.
manualExternalGates: MANUAL_PRODUCT / UX: before any AI Apply Assistant screen is implemented, UX and product owner must confirm the exact candidate panel/state subset that does not imply autonomous apply, resume/cover-letter processing or unsupported provider capability; CS-130 retains screen ownership. MANUAL_ACCESSIBILITY: run and record a real NVDA or VoiceOver smoke test on the implemented preparation control/result/error states. EXTERNAL_PROVIDER: any real provider acceptance is separate from this specification and must use disposable approved data; no provider call or deployment is authorized here.
risksRecovery: A stale client capability bit, sample design content or provider failure could falsely imply that an application feature is available or could leak sensitive data. Revert only the presentation boundary change, keep `AI_ENABLED` default-off and preserve existing preparation/domain state; do not change matching or application records.
definitionOfDone: Specification DoD: only the existing candidate preparation-coaching control is named as current capability; server session gating, owner scope, safe error/empty behavior, data exclusions, manual accessibility gate, CS-130 screen ownership, unknown route and non-blocking design limitation are explicit; all four source ACs have reviewed exact bindings; CONDITIONAL/default-off semantics remain unchanged. This specification performs no runtime implementation, provider activation or release action.

Future release DoD: exact CS-130 visual scope and tolerance receive UX/product approval; automated browser/accessibility/security evidence passes on an exact reviewed SHA; manual screen-reader evidence is recorded; any provider configuration and live acceptance are separately authorized and verified. AI remains unable to submit applications or alter deterministic matching.

relatedDesignScreenMapping.rationale: CS-100 specifies the candidate overview shell only. The desktop screen and mobile variant remain implementation-owned by CS-162 and CS-169 respectively; child detail/consent/provider screens and administrative panels are not reassigned to the parent.

1.setup: Record OS, screen-reader/browser/version, test build SHA, candidate role, route/component entry, fixture provenance and whether the state is pending, empty, unavailable, error, unauthorized or expired-session. Include expired-session only when the approved session/API contract exposes that state; otherwise record the exact contract basis for N/A. Use only sanitized synthetic view models; no provider account or real user data.
1.fixtureOrData: Synthetic candidate fixtures for pending, empty and unavailable/error/unauthorized states supported by the approved API contract; add expired-session only when that contract defines it. Never use the illustrative reference-board identity or status values.
1.action: Using only the screen reader and keyboard, navigate from the containing Settings context into the Connected Accounts overview, inspect the heading and list/status, traverse each actionable item (if authorized and implemented), and recover from each explicit unavailable/error state and contract-supported expired-session state.
1.procedure: Verify landmark/heading order announces Settings then Connected Accounts without an invented route claim; each account/status item has a unique accessible name and textual state derived from server data; pending/empty/unavailable/error/denied status is announced once and does not disclose account details when unauthorized. When the approved session/API contract exposes expired-session, verify its status is announced once, no account detail remains visible, focus moves or remains at the contract-defined recovery destination, and keyboard navigation can reach that destination; if the contract has no such rendered state, record N/A with its exact citation. Focus is visible, ordered and restored after any approved dialog; Tab/Shift+Tab and Escape behave as specified for implemented controls; no disabled/HOLD control is actionable. Record actual speech/keyboard result, defects and exact SHA; mark unsupported states N/A with the contract citation rather than passing them.
1.failureCase: If no authorized shell or supported API/session state exists, record BLOCKED/NOT RUN and preserve HOLD; never substitute axe or source inspection for manual AT evidence. If the approved session contract exposes expired-session UI but its status/contract-defined recovery destination is not announced or keyboard reachable, mark this manual criterion FAIL.
1.negativeCase: Any unannounced state, ambiguous control name, keyboard trap, lost focus, private account detail on denial or actionable held control fails. A contract-supported expired-session state that is not announced once, leaves account details visible or makes its recovery destination unreachable also fails.
